# Balanced Incomplete Block Designs and Alpha Designs

This project was completed by a team of four students. It brought together experimental-design theory, a practical agricultural or biological application, statistical analysis, model diagnostics, interpretation, and scientific communication.

::: {.agst-project-facts}
<div><span>TEAM</span><strong>4 collaborators</strong><p>Shared research, analysis, slide development, and presentation responsibilities.</p></div>
<div><span>FORMAT</span><strong>Recorded presentation</strong><p>The team presented the completed slide deck while recording the presentation.</p></div>
<div><span>DELIVERY</span><strong>YouTube submission</strong><p>The recording was published on YouTube and its link was shared with the professor for grading.</p></div>
:::

## Project focus

The work examined incomplete block designs, including balanced incomplete block designs (BIBD) and alpha designs. These designs are useful when a complete block cannot accommodate every treatment and the experiment must retain useful treatment comparisons under practical constraints.

## Assessed components

The course project rubric evaluates five connected areas:

1. Topic understanding and explanation
2. Exploratory analysis
3. Statistical analysis and diagnostics
4. Conclusions and recommendations
5. Presentation quality
